alarms.data_tree_path: GROUP: External Shutdown
alarms.long_description: External Pump Shutdown signal, XC7192, activated from ship system. PVU cannot operate.
alarms.cause: - Cause for shutdown external to PVU,\n- Failure in External Pump Shutdown signal, XC7192.
alarms.effect:
PVU pressure is blown down and PVU stopped.
PVU cannot operate before the failure situation is fixed.

1. Hydraulic pumps are stopped directly, and causes:
'Hydraulic Pump X Local/Failed' alarm,
'No Hyd. Pumps Available Trip Alarm'
2. Cryogenic pumps are stopped directly, and causes: 'Pump X Not Ok',
3. Control air pressure is dumped directly, and causes: 'Control Air Pressure Low' alarm.

As control air pressure is dumped, circulation valve V7050 is closed. This can cause a position failure, and cause 'Circ. Valve Pos. Dev. Trip Low' alarm.
alarms.suggested_action: - Check ships alarm system for cause for shutdown.\nIf cause is not ships system and/or associated alarms are not raised:\n - Check External Pump Shutdown signal, XC7192, NO contact, Closed during operation, and check cabling.

alarms.synopsis: MOP screens may show contents different from the system configuration
alarms.data_tree_path: MOP screens may show contents different from the system configuration
alarms.long_description: MOP screens may show contents different from the system configuration
alarms.cause: -  Configuration parameters changed, or\n -  During installation or upgrade, MOP rebooted before configurations parameters where loaded
alarms.effect: MOP screen labels and layout may be wrong or misleading.
alarms.suggested_action: Reboot MOP

alarms.synopsis: Service Engineer password has been used
alarms.data_tree_path: Service Engineer password has been used
alarms.long_description: Service Engineer password has been used
alarms.cause: -  The password has its initial (common) value, or\n-  MOP_SERVICE user has been logged in
alarms.effect: The password for the Service Engineer is not a secret
alarms.suggested_action:
In 'System Options' panel:
Change role to Chief
In 'Admin->About' panel:
Press 'Service Engineer Password', then press 'Generate new Service Engineer Password'
If the button is grayed out then Restart MOP, and repeat the procedure

alarms.synopsis: The NTP Time synchronization has failed
alarms.data_tree_path: The NTP Time synchronization has failed
alarms.long_description: Time is not being synchronized correctly from the clock server.
alarms.cause: The connection to the internet or the local network may be failing.
alarms.effect: This means that the time will not be set by the time server and clock accuracy has been downgraded.
alarms.suggested_action: Check that the internet connection and network devices are functioning correctly.

alarms.synopsis: MOP is running in the MOP_ADMIN account

alarms.cause: The MOP is running as MOP_ADMIN
alarms.effect: Not all parts of the MOP will be able to run correctly as MOP_ADMIN

alarms.data_tree_path: *->System->Service Terminal enabled
alarms.long_description: Serial service terminal interface access unlocked.
alarms.cause: A parameter has been set to enable service engineer access to the local service terminal interface on the controller.

alarms.data_tree_path: *->System->Invalid parameters
alarms.long_description: The PVCU1 Controller holds invalid parameters. The PVCU1 Controller cannot start its application without the correct parameters.
alarms.cause: The alarm is caused from the PVCU1 Controller automatically loads the wrong parameter set after a replacement of the PVCU1 Controller.
alarms.effect: The behaviour of the application in the PVCU1 Controller is not correct. The precise effect of this situation is unknown and care should be taken.
alarms.suggested_action: If the involved PVCU1 Controller just have been replaced, wait for the automatic preparation to complete. If this takes more than 10 minutes, the LED colour signalling for fault indication should be inspected. If this proves unhelpful, reset the PVCU1 Controller unit. If it still does not help, contact MAN-ES.

alarms.data_tree_path: *->System->Invalid software
alarms.long_description: PVCU1 Controller is running an incorrect application.
alarms.cause: MOP(s) not available during PVCU1 Controller power up.
alarms.effect:
Reduced system performance.

NOTE
Never ignore this alarm. Safety critical issues may arise!
alarms.suggested_action: Switch off PVCU1 Controller immediately.\nWhen MOP is available: Restart PVCU1 Controller.

alarms.data_tree_path: *->System->Invalid Parameter Flash
alarms.long_description: Parameter flash failure.
alarms.cause: The CRC check when reading the parameters from flash failed.
alarms.effect: Parameters from flash cannot be used.
alarms.suggested_action: Write a new parameter set to flash. If the problem persists, the unit may be defective.

alarms.data_tree_path: *->System->ID Key corrupt
alarms.long_description: The PVCU1 Controller cannot read ID-key data
alarms.cause:
- ID-key is not plugged in, or
- ID-key data is corrupted, or
- ID-key hardware failure, or
- PVCU1 Controller failure
alarms.effect: No immediate effect on performance.\nThe PVCU1 Controller may not function correctly after a restart.
alarms.suggested_action:
If this alarm is active for more than 5 minutes, check that the ID-key is plugged in correctly. 

If the problem persists replace, one at a time:
- ID-key (see instruction manual for configuration instructions) 
- PVCU1 Controller

alarms.data_tree_path: PVCU1->System->24V Power Supervision->ECS Insulation Level Supervision->ECS Insulation level below normal
alarms.long_description: PVCU1 electric insulation level is below normal service value.
alarms.cause: One or more components connected to PVCU1 have increased electric leakage to ships ground.
alarms.effect: No immediate effect. The alarm can be an indication of beginning deterioration of system components.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Insulation level by observing: Maintenance -> Troubleshooting -> Insulation,
- Insulation level trend in CoCoS-EDS if applicable,
- Individual insulation of PVCU1 components (sensors, controllers, actuators, cabling) to determine the cause of leakage.

alarms.data_tree_path: PVCU1->System->24V Power Supervision->ECS Insulation Level Supervision->ECS Insulation level too low
alarms.long_description: PVCU1 electric insulation level is too low.
alarms.cause: One or more components connected to PVCU1 have too high electric leakage to ships ground.
alarms.effect:
- The systems resistance against electrical noise is reduced.
- Additional insulation faults on opposite polarity can cause blown fuses or short circuits.
NOTE:
Never ignore this alarm. Safety critical issues may arise.
alarms.suggested_action:
NOTE:
Never ignore this alarm. Safety critical issues may arise.
Check:
- Insulation level by observing : Maintenance -> Troubleshooting -> Insulation,
- Insulation level trend in CoCoS-EDS if applicable,
- Individual insulation of PVCU1 components (sensors, controllers, actuators, cabling) to determine the cause of leakage.

alarms.data_tree_path: *->System->24V Power Supervision->Noise Detector->Electrical noise detected
alarms.long_description: Electrical noise has been detected in the PVU-CS system
alarms.cause: - One or more PVU-CS components has intermittent and/or oscillating electric leakage to ship's ground, or\n- PVU-CS system has been subjected to electrical noise from an external source.
alarms.effect:
No immediate effect
The fault can generate other consequential alarms in the PVU-CS system, e.g. 
- Pump X piston speed alarms
- Fluctuating sensor measurements and alarms

NOTE: 
Never ignore this alarm. Safety critical issues may arise.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Noise pulse counter by observing : Maintenance -> Troubleshooting -> Insulation
- Cabling, sensors, actuators, Controllers for loose connections or intermittent and/or oscillating electric leakages/short circuits to ground.

To locate an intermittent and/or oscillating electric leakage to ship's ground:
1.Engine should run on fuel oil
2. Set the PVCU1 Controller in TEST MODE by pressing the Mode button on MOP Maintenance -> System view
I/O. This will stop the controllers normal function.
3. Disconnect connections one at a time (except for the power cable), and after each disconnection observe if
increase in noise pulse counter has stopped
4. If increase has stopped, the cable, sensor or actuator with loose connections or intermittent and/or
oscillating electric leakages/short circuits to ground, has been located
5.Revert to basic electrical trouble shooting to repair
6.Set the PVCU1 Controller in NORNAL MODE by pressing the Mode button on MOP Maintenance -> System view I/O.

alarms.data_tree_path: *->System->24V Power Supervision->24V power A failure
alarms.long_description: Power supply failure on PVCU1, terminal X9, VA.
alarms.cause: Power supply voltage out of normal range.
alarms.effect:
If power supply B is working:
- No effect on engine performance.
- No power supply redundancy on PVCU1.

If both power supply A and B are failing:
- PVCU1 will be switched off or are running with low voltage.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Power supply A.
- Voltage on power module terminal X9, VA
- Cabling.

alarms.data_tree_path: *->System->24V Power Supervision->PD ch 1 Fuse failure
alarms.long_description: Power failure on PVCU1 power distribution module, terminal X1.
alarms.cause:
- Overcurrent.
- Short circuit.
- Faulty sensor(s)/actuator(s).

If alarm occurs together with "PD input power detected", input voltage is detected on power distribution module, terminal X1.
alarms.effect: No power is supplied from terminal X1.\n\nIf alarm occurs together with "PD input power detected", see effect from "PD input power detected" alarm info.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Cabling
- Connected sensor(s)/actuator(s) for malfunction(s) (too high current load).

Reset the fuse on terminal X1 via the display on the CPU module:
- <Right> key to enter "Service"
- <Down> key to enter "Fuse, DO & AO"
- <Enter> key enter "Reactivate all fuses after error"
- <Enter> key to re-activate fuses

Note: If alarm occurs together with "PD input power detected", see suggested action from "PD input power detected" alarm info.

alarms.data_tree_path: PVCU1->System->24V Power Supervision->1390-PS-Failed Channel
alarms.long_description: I/O Channel Failed.
alarms.cause: Hardware failure in the I/O channel.
alarms.effect: May reduce performance.
alarms.suggested_action:
Try the steps below until OK. For each step check whether the error has disappeared:
   1) Check that all screws holding the modules are securely fastened
   2) Replace the corresponding module
   3) Replace CPU module
   4) Replace the controller frame, containing the back plane.

alarms.data_tree_path: PVCU1->System->24V Power Supervision->1390-PS-Module unavail.
alarms.long_description: I/O Module Unavailable
alarms.cause: Module is not connected correct or Module has damaged HW.
alarms.effect: May reduce performance.
alarms.suggested_action: Replace corresponding Triton module.

alarms.synopsis: PS manio error, PS not activated
alarms.data_tree_path: *->System->PS manio error, PS not activated
alarms.long_description: The communication between CPU and Power Supervision modules does not work.
alarms.cause: The FPGAs on the CPU and PS are incompatible, or HW error.
alarms.effect: The PS module can be divided into "power supply" and "power supervision".\nWhen the communication fails, the power supervision part does not work.
alarms.suggested_action:
Update the PS FPGA if alarm for Incorrect FPGA version, otherwise
try the steps below until OK. For each step check whether the error has disappeared:
   1) Check that all screws holding the modules are securely fastened
   2) Replace power supervision module
   3) Replace CPU module
 4) Replace the controller frame, containing the back plane

alarms.data_tree_path: *->System->Incorrect FPGA version
alarms.long_description: Incorrect FPGA version.
alarms.cause: The modules FPGA does not match the expected FPGA version.
alarms.effect: The controller can not start up in normal mode.
alarms.suggested_action: Upgrade the FPGA by restarting the node when connected to a MOP.

alarms.data_tree_path: *->System->Mismatching SW/FPGA images on MOP's
alarms.long_description: MOP A/B do not have same SW version
alarms.cause: The ECS-SW or FPGA Load SW are not the same on MOP A/B
alarms.effect: Automatic update of SW/FPGA via the MOP will not work
alarms.suggested_action: Check the SW installation on MOP A/B and update the ECS SW or FPGA load SW .\nA force download from one MOP will start the update process from that MOP

alarms.data_tree_path: *->System->PTP Status->NET-A P2Pdel too large
alarms.long_description: NET A P2P delay too large.
alarms.cause: Incorrect setup of the network switches.\nDefect switch or port on switch.\nDefect CPU module
alarms.effect: The nodes are not able to synchronize with the PTP master.\nMay reduce performance.
alarms.suggested_action:
If this happens to more nodes connected to the same NET A switch:
   1) update the setup of the switch
   2) replace the switch

If this is the only node try each step below to see whether the problem disappears:
   1) connect the Controllers NET A connector to another port on the NET A switch
   2) replace the involved switch
   3) replace the CPU module

alarms.cause: Incorrect setup of the network switches.\nDefect switch or port on switch.\nDefect CPU module
alarms.effect: The nodes are not able to synchronize with the PTP master.\nMay reduce performance.
alarms.suggested_action:
If this happens to more nodes connected to the same NET B switch:
  1) update the setup of the switch
   2) replace the switch

If this is the only node try each step below to see whether the problem disappears:
   1) connect the Controllers NET B connector to another port on the NET B switch
   2) replace the involved switch
   3) replace the CPU module

alarms.data_tree_path: *->System->PTP Status->PTP clock not synchronized
alarms.long_description: PTP clock is not synchronized with PTP master.
alarms.cause: Incorrect setup of the network switches.\nDefect switch or port on switch.\nDefect CPU module
alarms.effect: May reduce performance.
alarms.suggested_action:
If this happens to more nodes connected to the same switch:
  1) update the setup of the switch
  2) replace the switch

If this is the only node try each step below to see whether the problem disappears:
   1) connect the controller net cable to another port on the net switch. Only connect the Controllers NET A connector with NET A switch, and the Controllers NET B connector with NET B switch
   2) replace the involved switch
   3) replace the CPU module

alarms.effect: May reduce performance.

alarms.data_tree_path: PVCU1->Pump Monitoring->Pistons Speed and Pos Monitoring->Pump 1->Pump 1 Position
alarms.long_description: Pump 1 Piston Position signal XC7082-1 is not within correct range.
alarms.cause:
- Pump 1 Piston Position sensor, XC7082-1 
- - Incorrect calibration, calibration may have drifted.
- - Cabling failure, 
- - Cable short circuit, 
- - Power supply failure to sensor amplifier,
- - Sensor failure,
- - Sensor amplifier failure,
- - Ex-barrier failure, 
- MPC input channel failure.
alarms.effect:
- PVU has changed to Stand-by Fail state, if it was in operation. 
- or PVU was stopped, if it was in preparing sequence state.
PVU cannot be started until the failure is remedied, 

or Pump 1 is Blocked.
alarms.suggested_action:
Stop PVU.
- Check calibration of Pump 1 Piston Position sensor, XC7082-1  
- Check Cabling, 
- Check electric power to sensor,
- Check sensor,
- Check output current of sensor amplifier,
- Check MPC input channel. 

Alternatively: Deactivate pump 1 

If the problem persists: Replace MPC.

alarms.data_tree_path: PVCU1->Pump Monitoring->Pistons Speed and Pos Monitoring->Pump 1->Pump 1 Forward Speed High
alarms.long_description: Pump 1 Piston forward speed high.
alarms.cause:
- Vaporized gas in LNG pump 1 chamber,
- - LNG Pump 1 chamber not cold enough,
- - - Cooling circulation flow too low,
- - LNG temperature too high and /or pressure too low,
- - Too low LNG flow to pump 1 
- PVU discharge flow too high,
- Hydraulic pressure too high,
- Air in hydraulic oil,
- Failure or wear of LNG pump 1 
- Failure of LNG pump 1 piston position sensor, ZT7082-1 or amplifier.
alarms.effect: Alarm - continued operation.
alarms.suggested_action:
View Trouble Shooting -> Piston Events for stored log of piston movement.
If continuing:
A. Pump 1 can be cut-off and operation reactivated using only 2 pumps.
B. Stop PVU and prepare it for maintenance /trouble-shooting. 
- Check circulation temperature, TE7058-1, 
- Check filter F7010 and positions of valves in the circulation loop,
- Check position function of Circulation Valve, V7050,
- Check orifices of pump 1, 
- Check LNG inlet pressure, TT7024 and pressure, PT7023,
- Check if discharge flow of PVU is higher than max., e.g. caused by leaking gas,
- Check hydraulic pressure, PT7084, and operation of hydraulic power supply,
- Check for air in hydraulic oil,
- Check piston rings of LNG pump 1 piston, 
- Check suction valve of LNG pump 1,
- Check LNG pump 1 piston position sensor, ZT7082-1 or amplifier.

alarms.data_tree_path: PVCU1->Pump Monitoring->Pistons Speed and Pos Monitoring->Pump 1->Pump 1 Not Returning
alarms.long_description: Pump 1 piston did not return within time limit. PVU cannot operate.
alarms.cause:
- Low pressure hydraulic oil pressure, PT7087, too low,
- Dirt, water or air in hydraulic oil or in pump 1 hydraulic actuator or activation valve, V7081-1 
- Failure of Pump 1 Activation Valve, V7081-1 
- Pump 1 hydraulic actuator piston or LNG pump piston is sticking, e.g. caused by seizing,
- Failure of Pump 1 Piston Position sensor, XC7082-1  measurement,
- Failure of Pumps Return Flow Limit control.
alarms.effect: - If PVU was in operation, PVU is blown down and stopped.
alarms.suggested_action:
A. Pump 1 can be cut-off and operation reactivated using only 2 pumps.
B. Stop PVU and prepare it for maintenance /trouble-shooting. 
- Check LP hydraulic pressure, PT7087,
- Check hydraulic oil for contamination with dirt, water or air,
- Check power to Pump 1 Activation Valve V7081-1 
- Check function of Pump 1 Activation Valve V7081-1 
- Check Pump 1 Intermediate Chamber Temperature, TT7094-1 
- Check if Pump 1 hydraulic actuator piston and LNG pump piston can move freely,
- Check Pump 1 Piston Position sensor XC7082-1  calibration and cabling,
- Check Pumps Return Flow Limit output signal, PVCU1 ch. 71, XC70811, and cabling to all 3 valves V7081-1/2/3.

- Vaporized gas in LNG pump 3 chamber, 
- - LNG pump 3 chamber not cold enough, 
- - - Cooling circulation flow too low, 
- - LNG temperature too high and /or pressure too low, 
- Air in hydraulic oil, 
- Failure of LNG pump 3 piston position sensor, ZT7082-3 or amplifier,
- Failure in control of piston,
- Leakages from pump discharge to suction.
alarms.effect: PVU has changed to Stand-by Fail state.\nIf no problems can be identified, PVU can be restarted by pressing Standby button.
alarms.suggested_action:
View Trouble Shooting -> Piston Events for stored log of piston movement.
A. PVU can be restarted again by pressing "Standby" button, if a possible cause cannot be observed (e.g. by measurements or other alarms). 
If the failure happens again observe measurements.
B. Pump 3 can be cut-off and operation reactivated using only 2 pumps.
C. Stop PVU and prepare it for maintenance / trouble-shooting. 
- Check circulation temperature, TE7058-3, 
- Check filter F7010 and positions of valves in the circulation loop,
- Check orifices of pump 3 
- Check position function of Circulation Valve, V7050,
- Check LNG inlet pressure , TT7024 and pressure, PT7023,
- Check if discharge flow of PVU is higher than max., e.g. caused by leaking gas,
- Check LP hydraulic pressure, PT7087,
- Check for air in hydraulic oil,
- Check discharge check valve of LNG pump 3,
- Check PVCU1 ch. 71, XC70811, pumps return flow limit, and cabling,
- Check LNG pump 3 piston position sensor, ZT7082-3 or amplifier.

alarms.data_tree_path: PVCU1->Pump Monitoring->Pistons Speed and Pos Monitoring->Pump 3->Pump 3 Not Returning
alarms.long_description: Pump 3 piston did not return within time limit. PVU cannot operate.
alarms.cause:
- Low pressure hydraulic oil pressure, PT7087, too low,
- Dirt, water or air in hydraulic oil or in pump 3 hydraulic actuator or activation valve, V7081-3 
- Failure of Pump 3 Activation Valve, V7081-3 
- Pump 3 hydraulic actuator piston or LNG pump piston is sticking, e.g. caused by seizing,
- Failure of Pump 3 Piston Position sensor, XC7082-3  measurement,
- Failure of Pumps Return Flow Limit control.
alarms.effect: - If PVU was in operation, PVU is blown down and stopped.
alarms.suggested_action:
A. Pump 3 can be cut-off and operation reactivated using only 2 pumps.
B. Stop PVU and prepare it for maintenance /trouble-shooting. 
- Check LP hydraulic pressure, PT7087,
- Check hydraulic oil for contamination with dirt, water or air,
- Check power to Pump 3 Activation Valve V7081-3 
- Check function of Pump 3 Activation Valve V7081-3 
- Check Pump 3 Intermediate Chamber Temperature, TT7094-3 
- Check if Pump 3 hydraulic actuator piston and LNG pump piston can move freely,
- Check Pump 3 Piston Position sensor XC7082-3  calibration and cabling,
- Check Pumps Return Flow Limit output signal, PVCU1 ch. 71, XC70811, and cabling to all 3 valves V7081-1/2/3.

alarms.data_tree_path: PVCU1->Pump Monitoring->Pistons Sticking Monitoring->Piston 1 is Sticking
alarms.long_description: Pump 1 Piston is returning too slow.
alarms.cause: Pump 1 Piston has been moved too deep into the 100 mm brake damper, and did not revert in due time.
alarms.effect: Alarm - continued operation.\n
alarms.suggested_action:
View Trouble Shooting -> Piston Events for stored log of piston movement.
 If continuing or severe sticking failure:
A. Recalibrate Pump 1 position sensor.
B. Pump 1 can be cut-off and operation reactivated using only 2 pumps.

alarms.data_tree_path: PVCU2->System->24V Power Supervision->ECS Insulation Level Supervision->ECS Insulation level below normal
alarms.long_description: PVCU2 electric insulation level is below normal service value.
alarms.cause: One or more components connected to PVCU2 have increased electric leakage to ships ground.
alarms.effect: No immediate effect. The alarm can be an indication of beginning deterioration of system components.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Insulation level by observing: Maintenance -> Troubleshooting -> Insulation,
- Insulation level trend in CoCoS-EDS if applicable,
- Individual insulation of PVCU2 components (sensors, controllers, actuators, cabling) to determine the cause of leakage.

alarms.data_tree_path: PVCU2->System->24V Power Supervision->ECS Insulation Level Supervision->ECS Insulation level too low
alarms.long_description: PVCU2 electric insulation level is too low.
alarms.cause: One or more components connected to PVCU2 have too high electric leakage to ships ground.
alarms.effect:
- The systems resistance against electrical noise is reduced.
- Additional insulation faults on opposite polarity can cause blown fuses or short circuits.
NOTE:
Never ignore this alarm. Safety critical issues may arise.
alarms.suggested_action:
NOTE:
Never ignore this alarm. Safety critical issues may arise.
Check:
- Insulation level by observing : Maintenance -> Troubleshooting -> Insulation,
- Insulation level trend in CoCoS-EDS if applicable,
- Individual insulation of PVCU2 components (sensors, controllers, actuators, cabling) to determine the cause of leakage.

alarms.data_tree_path: PVCU2->System->24V Power Supervision->1390-PS-Failed Channel
alarms.long_description: I/O Channel Failed.
alarms.cause: Hardware failure in the I/O channel.
alarms.effect: May reduce performance.
alarms.suggested_action:
Try the steps below until OK. For each step check whether the error has disappeared:
   1) Check that all screws holding the modules are securely fastened
   2) Replace the corresponding module
   3) Replace CPU module
   4) Replace the controller frame, containing the back plane.

alarms.data_tree_path: PVCU2->System->24V Power Supervision->1390-PS-Module unavail.
alarms.long_description: I/O Module Unavailable
alarms.cause: Module is not connected correct or Module has damaged HW.
alarms.effect: May reduce performance.
alarms.suggested_action: Replace corresponding Triton module.

alarms.data_tree_path: PVCU2->System->Modbus Interface->Modbus Slave failure
alarms.long_description: PVU - FGSS communication failure.
alarms.cause:
- Cable failure, 
- FGSS failure, 
- PVU Modbus failure, 
- Commissioning error.
alarms.effect: Information on FGSS displays and remote Start / Stop of PVU are lost.\nIt may not be possible to start PVU.
alarms.suggested_action:
- Check communcation cable,
- Check FGSS communication unit, possibly restart unit,
- Restart MPC: PVCU2 in PVU-CS. 

If cabling is OK and restarts did not fix problem: Replace PVCU2.

alarms.data_tree_path: PVCU2->System->Modbus Interface->Modbus Version->Modbus Interface Version Alarm
alarms.long_description: Interface Version Number used by PVU-CS and FGSS does not match. \nInterface Version Number is used to check that PVU-CS and FGSS use same definition of data on the Modbus communication line.
alarms.cause: SW of PVU-CS and FGSS do not contain same Modbus communication interface version.
alarms.effect: All data received on Modbus line is marked invalid, until the Interface Version Numbers on PVU-CS and FGSS sides match.
alarms.suggested_action: - Check that Interface Version Number for the specific plant is correct and the same in both PVU-CS and FGSS.\n- If Interface Version Number is not correct in the FGSS, please contact the FGSS supplier for setting up the system correctly.\n- If Interface Version Number not correct in the PVU-CS, please contact MAN Energy Solutions, Copenhagen.

alarms.data_tree_path: PVCU2->System->Modbus Interface->Modbus Version->Modbus Configuration no. Alarm
alarms.long_description: Configuration Number used by PVU-CS and FGSS does not match. \nConfiguration Number is used to check that PVU-CS and FGSS use same configuration of data on the Modbus communication line.
alarms.cause: SW of PVU-CS and FGSS are not customized to same Modbus communication configuration.
alarms.effect: Some data transmitted on Modbus line might not be updated or might not be correct, as long as Configuration Numbers on PVU-CS and FGSS do not match.\nIt is not recommended to use the PVU before the mismatch is fixed.
alarms.suggested_action:
- Contact MAN Energy Solutions to get Configuration Number for the specific plant.
- Check that Configuration Number for the specific plant is correct and the same in both PVU-CS and FGSS.
- If Configuration Number is not correct in the FGSS, please contact the FGSS supplier for setting up the system correctly.
- If Configuration Number not correct in the PVU-CS, please contact MAN Energy Solutions, Copenhagen.

alarms.long_description: No I/O connection.
alarms.cause:

- Sensor failure, or
- Supervision resistor across the switch is missing, or 
- PVCU2 Controller input channel failure
alarms.effect: Reduced supervision. May reduce performance.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Cabling
- Sensor
- Supervision resistor 
- PVCU2 Controller input channel: 'Maintenance' -> 'System View I/O Test'

If the problem persists: Replace the corresponding module on PVCU2

alarms.data_tree_path: PVCU2->IO Configuration->AI,6005-1,ME1 SF Press SP->6005-1-ME1 SF Press SP-Failed Channel
alarms.long_description: I/O Channel Failed.
alarms.cause: Hardware failure in the I/O channel.
alarms.effect: May reduce performance.
alarms.suggested_action:
Try the steps below until OK. For each step check whether the error has disappeared:
   1) Check that all screws holding the modules are securely fastened
   2) Replace the corresponding module
   3) Replace CPU module
   4) Replace the controller frame, containing the back plane.

alarms.data_tree_path: PVCU2->PVU Control->PVU State Machine->PVU in Manual Mode
alarms.long_description: PVU is in Manual Mode. Certain actuators and subsystems can be controlled manually. Note: Consult the PVU user manual before operating actuators and subsystems in Manual Mode.
alarms.cause: User switched PVU Mode to Manual.
alarms.effect: Monitoring partly disabled.\nPVU cannot receive Standby requests.
alarms.suggested_action: Switch PVU Mode to Auto.

alarms.data_tree_path: PVCU2->PVU Control->PVU State Machine->Stand-by State Timeout Stop
alarms.long_description: PVU has been stopped after Stand-by State timeout.
alarms.cause: - PVU has exceeded the time limit for being in Stand-by State.\n- PVU has exceeded the time limit for performing manual pressurizations.
alarms.effect: PVU has been stopped.
alarms.suggested_action: Restart PVU in due time before necessary for gas supply to main engine.

alarms.data_tree_path: PVCU2->PVU Control->PVU State Machine->Shutdown to Stand-by Fail State
alarms.long_description: PVU is shutdown to Stand-by Fail state.
alarms.cause: A failure has occurred which prevent PVU from operating.
alarms.effect: PVU has changed to Stand-by Fail state, if it was operating,\nPVU cannot operate before the failure situation is remedied.
alarms.suggested_action: - Check Alarm List for alarm indicating cause for shutdown.

alarms.data_tree_path: PVCU2->PVU Control->PVU State Machine->Shutdown, Blowdown to Stop
alarms.long_description: PVU is shutdown, gas pressure blowdown and stopped.
alarms.cause: A failure has occurred which prevent PVU from operating.
alarms.effect: PVU pressure is blown down and PVU stopped.\nPVU cannot operate before the failure situation is fixed.
alarms.suggested_action: - Check Alarm List for alarm indicating cause for shutdown.

alarms.data_tree_path: PVCU2->PVU Control->PVU State Machine->Shutdown to Blowdown Fail State
alarms.long_description: PVU is shutdown and locked in Blowdown fail state.
alarms.cause: During blowdown Inlet Valve, V7012, does not close as commanded.
alarms.effect: PVU is shutdown but locked in Blowdown fail state with Blowdown Valve, V7033, closed, to prevent LNG to flow to the vent pipe.
alarms.suggested_action: - Close PVU LNG inlet by manual valve HV7015.

alarms.data_tree_path: PVCU2->PVU Control->PVU State Machine->PVU Outlet Pressurize Timeout
alarms.long_description: Too long time to pressurize PVU, PVU outlet Pressure, PT7077 to engine gas pressure setpoint
alarms.cause:
- Leakage of PVU or gas pipe or valves,
- Reduced capacity of PVU,
- - PVU pumps might not be cold enough,
- Loss of hydraulic oil flow,
- - Air in hydraulic oil,
- - N2 in hydraulic oil caused by leaking hydraulic accumulators,
- - Hydraulic oil leakage,
- - Failure in hydraulic pump control,
- Failure of PVU Outlet Pressure measurement, PT7077.
alarms.effect: PVU has changed to Stand-by Fail state, if it was operating,\nPVU cannot operate before the failure situation is remedied.
alarms.suggested_action:
- Check if PVU Outlet Pressure, PT7077, is approx. constant when PVU is in Standby Fail state,
- Check for abnormal behavior of PVU,
- Crosscheck PVU Outlet Pressure measurement, PT7077, against PT7025 and PT6017 of the GVT.

Stop PVU:
- Check N2 pressure of hydraulic accumulators,
- Check hydraulic oil high pressure pipe between HPS and PVU,
- Function check Hydraulic Power Supply unit,
- Check gas high pressure pipe between PVU and engine.

alarms.data_tree_path: PVCU2->PVU Control->PVU State Machine->Pressurize to Pipe Pressure Timeout
alarms.long_description: Too long time to pressurize PVU, PVU outlet Pressure, PT7077, to supply pipe pressure, PT6017.
alarms.cause:
- Leakage of PVU or gas pipe or valves,
- Reduced capacity of PVU,
- - PVU pumps might not be cold enough,
- Loss of hydraulic oil flow,
- - Air in hydraulic oil,
- - N2 in hydraulic oil caused by leaking hydraulic accumulators,
- - Hydraulic oil leakage,
- - Failure in hydraulic pump control.
- Failure of PVU Outlet Pressure measurement, PT7077,
- Failure of Supply Pipe Pressure measurement, PT6017.
alarms.effect: PVU has changed to Stand-by Fail state, if it was operating,\nPVU cannot operate before the failure situation is remedied.
alarms.suggested_action:
- Check if PVU Outlet Pressure, PT7077, is approx. constant when PVU is in Standby Fail state,
- Check for abnormal behavior of PVU,
- Crosscheck PVU Outlet Pressure measurement, PT7077, against PT7025 and PT6017 of the GVT.

Stop PVU:
- Check N2 pressure of hydraulic accumulators,
- Check hydraulic oil high pressure pipe between HPS and PVU,
- Function check Hydraulic Power Supply unit,
- Check gas high pressure pipe between PVU and engine.

alarms.data_tree_path: PVCU2->PVU Control->Hydraulic Control->Hydraulic Pumps Control->Hydraulic Pump Unit 1->Hydraulic Pump 1 Not Responding
alarms.long_description: Hydraulic Pump 1 is commanded to operate, but does not run.
alarms.cause: - Hydraulic Pump 1 power supply may be Off,\n- Hydraulic Pump 1 electric motor may be overloaded,\n- Failure in PVU-CS output XC7107-1.
alarms.effect: - The hydraulic pump cannot be controlled from PVU-CS.\n- PVU discharge is limited,\n- If there is no hydraulic pumps ready, the PVU cannot run.
alarms.suggested_action: - Check power to hydraulic pump starter box,\n- Check if there is a failure in the hydraulic pump starter box,\n- Check PVU-CS output XC7107-1 or cabling.

alarms.data_tree_path: PVCU2->PVU Control->Hydraulic Control->Hydraulic Pumps Control->Hydraulic Pump Unit 1->Hydraulic Pump 1 Local/Failed
alarms.long_description: Hydraulic pump 1 is in local control mode or has failed.
alarms.cause: The hydraulic pump has been changed from remote to local control, or has been stopped due to a failure.
alarms.effect: - The hydraulic pump cannot be controlled from PVU-CS.\n- PVU discharge is limited,\n- If there is no hydraulic pumps ready, the PVU cannot run.
alarms.suggested_action: - Check if there is a failure in the hydraulic pump starter box.\n- If deemed safe, change the hydraulic pump to remote mode.

alarms.data_tree_path: PVCU2->PVU Control->Hydraulic Control->Hydraulic Pumps Control->Hydraulic Pump Unit 1->Hydraulic Pump 1 Started No CMD
alarms.long_description: Hydraulic Pump 1 is running, but not commanded to operate by PVU-CS.
alarms.cause: - Hydraulic Pump 1 may be started locally,\n- Hydraulic Pump 1 starter box may have an electrical failure,\n- Failure in PVU-CS output XC7107-1.
alarms.effect: - The hydraulic pump and pressure cannot be controlled.
alarms.suggested_action:
- Stop the hydraulic pump 1 locally on starter box,
- Check local control in hydraulic pump starter box,
- Check if there is a failure in the hydraulic pump starter box,
- Check if failure of PVU-CS output XC7107-1.

alarms.data_tree_path: PVCU2->PVU Control->Hydraulic Control->Hydraulic Pumps Control->Hydraulic Pump Unit 2->Hydraulic Pump 2 Not Responding
alarms.long_description: Hydraulic Pump 2 is commanded to operate, but does not run.
alarms.cause: - Hydraulic Pump 2 power supply may be Off,\n- Hydraulic Pump 2 electric motor may be overloaded,\n- Failure in PVU-CS output XC7107-2.

- A manual valve in LNG supply piping are Closed by mistake,
- A manual valve in LNG supply piping are Open to vent by mistake,
- A pressure relief is leaking,

alarms.effect: PVU has changed to Stand-by Fail state, if it was operating,\nor PVU is stopped, if it was in preparing sequence state.\nPVU cannot operate before the failure situation is remedied.

- Check tank supply pump,
- Check if manual valve, HV7015, is Closed by mistake,
- Check if manual valve, HV7017, is Open by mistake,
- Check if manual valve, HV7006, is Open by mistake and is leaking,
- Check if manual valve, HV7065, is Open by mistake,
- Check if manual valve, HV7059, is Open by mistake,
- Check if valves in LNG supply piping are closed by mistake,
- Check if pressure relief valves, PSV7018, PSV7015, PSV7055, PCV7059 or PSV7054 are leaking,
- Check  PVU LNG Inlet Press sensor, PT7023, and cabling.

alarms.long_description: PVU Outlet Pressure PT7077 is significantly lower than GVT Engine Supply Pipe Pressure PT6017. PVU tripped.
alarms.cause: - Failure of PT7077 PVU Outlet Pressure measurement.\n- Failure of PT6017 GVT Engine Supply Pipe Pressure measurement.
alarms.effect: PVU has changed to Stand-by Fail state, if it was operating,\nPVU cannot operate before the failure situation is remedied.
alarms.suggested_action:
Stop the PVU.
- Check if test valves for the sensors are in correct positions,
- Check the PVU Outlet Pressure sensor (PT7077) and cabling,
- Check the GVT Engine Supply Pipe Pressure Sensor (PT6017) and cabling.

- Release pressure of supply pipe (- to be done from ships control system),
- Check Supply Pipe Pressure sensor (PT6017) and cabling.

alarms.long_description: Hydraulic Oil Inlet Pressure, PT7084, is too high to operate.
alarms.cause:
- HPS valve 641 was not activated (not open) during hydraulic oil heating,
- - Failure of Hyd. Oil Heating Valve Control signal, XC7106,
- Too large displacement of Hydraulic Pump:
- - Failure of Hyd. Pump Displacement SP output, XC7110-x, of the running hydraulic pump(s),
- - Failure in hyd. pump control valve,
- Failure of Hydraulic Inlet Pressure measurement, PT7084.
alarms.effect: HPS hydraulic pumps are stopped. PVU has changed to Stand-by Fail state, if it was operating,\nPVU cannot operate before the failure situation is remedied.
alarms.suggested_action:
Start function check of Hydraulic Power Supply, with low displacement:
- Crosscheck Hydraulic Supply pressure, PT7111, and PVU Hydraulic Oil Inlet Pressure, PT7084,
- Check if HPS valve 641 is activated (open), signal XC7106 and cabling,
- Check Hyd. Pump Displacement SP output, XC7110-x, of the running hydraulic pump(s) and cabling,
- Check one hyd. pump at a time and observe if they operate equally,
- Check Hydraulic Supply Pressure sensor, PT7084, and cabling.

alarms.long_description: Hydraulic Oil Tank Temperature A (TT7103-A) too low for operation.
alarms.cause:
- Cold conditions and hydraulic oil could not be heated within set time, 
- Failure of oil circulation heating:
- - Hydraulic pressure, PT7111, is too low,
- - Flow through orifice 642 of Hydraulic Power Supply is too low,
- Too much cooling of oil in HPS cooler 705,
- Failure of temperature measurements, TT7103-A or TT7103-B.
alarms.effect: PVU has changed to Stand-by Fail state, if it was operating,\nPVU cannot operate before the failure situation is remedied.
alarms.suggested_action:
- Check if one or more hydraulic pumps are running,
- Check if Hydraulic Oil Heating valve, XC7106, is activated,
- Check for too high water flow in HPS cooler 705,
- Check position of manual valve, HV70851,
- Check if PCV7086 and PSV7089 are leaking,
- Check if HPS safety valve 311 is leaking,
- Check if temperature measurements, TT7103-A or TT7103-B, are different.

alarms.data_tree_path: PVCU2->PVU Failure Handling->Pumps->Pump 1->Pump 1 Not Ok->Pump 1 Not Ok
alarms.long_description: The positions of valves HV7026-1 and HV7029-1  and power state of control valve V7081-1 of PVU Pump 1 do not match the selected mode: Active or Blocked. PVU cannot operate.
alarms.cause:
- PVU Pump 1 is selected Active, but valves HV7026-1 or HV7029-1 are closed, or power to control valve V7081-1 is removed,
- PVU Pump 1 is selected Blocked, but valves HV7026-1 or HV7029-1 are open, or power to control valve V7081-1 is On.
- Failure of valve signals,
- Failure in shutdown signal from ships Gas Safety System to all PVU control valves, V7081.
alarms.effect: - If PVU was in operation, it has changed to Stand-by Fail state and cannot operate before pump 1 is correctly activated or cut-off.\n- If PVU was stopped, it cannot be started until pump 1 is correctly activated or cut-off.
alarms.suggested_action:
- Correct positions of valves HV7026-1 and HV7029-1 
- Correct power connector to Pump 1 Activation Valve V7081-1 
If this does not fix the situation, Stop PVU.
- Check cables for valves HV7026-1 and HV7029-1 
- Check power to Pump 1 Activation Valve V7081-1 
- Check function of Pump 1 Activation Valve V7081-1 
- Check for failure in Pump 1 Activation Valve OK status signal, XC7083-1 or cabling.
- Check shutdown signal and cabling from ships Gas Safety System to all PVU control valves, V7081.
- Check hydraulic oil for contamination with dirt, water or air,

alarms.long_description: Pump 2 Circulation Temperature, 7058-2   is not low enough to operate.
alarms.cause:
- Too low LNG cooling flow through pump.
- - Manual valves HV7015 or HV7053 partly or fully closed,
- - Manual valves HV7026-2 or HV7029-2 partly or fully closed, 
- - Failure of Circulation Valve, V7050, control,
- - Return pipe to tank is partly or fully blocked, e.g. valves closed,
- - Orifices inside or after pump 2 clogged,
- Failure of Pump 2 Circulation Temperature, 7058-2  measurement.
alarms.effect: - If PVU was in operation, it has changed to Standby-fail state.\n- PVU cannot be started until pump 2 is sufficiently cooled.
alarms.suggested_action:
- Check position of manual valves HV7015 or HV7053,
- Check position of manual valves HV7026-2 or HV7029-2   
- Check positon of valves in return pipe to tank,
Stop PVU:
- Check function of Circulation Valve, V7050,
- Check the Pump 2 Circulation Temperature sensor, 7058-2  and cabling,
- Check  if orifices inside or after pump 2 are clogged,
Pump 2 can be blocked to get the PVU in operation using only 2 pumps.

alarms.data_tree_path: PVCU2->PVU Failure Handling->Pumps->Pump 3->Pump 3 Not Ok->Pump 3 Not Ok
alarms.long_description: The positions of valves HV7026-3 and HV7029-3  and power state of control valve V7081-3 of PVU Pump 3 do not match the selected mode: Active or Blocked. PVU cannot operate.
alarms.cause:
- PVU Pump 3 is selected Active, but valves HV7026-3 or HV7029-3 are closed, or power to control valve V7081-3 is removed,
- PVU Pump 3 is selected Blocked, but valves HV7026-3 or HV7029-3 are open, or power to control valve V7081-3 is On.
- Failure of valve signals,
- Failure in shutdown signal from ships Gas Safety System to all PVU control valves, V7081.
alarms.effect: - If PVU was in operation, it has changed to Stand-by Fail state and cannot operate before pump 3 is correctly activated or cut-off.\n- If PVU was stopped, it cannot be started until pump 3 is correctly activated or cut-off.
alarms.suggested_action:
- Correct positions of valves HV7026-3 and HV7029-3 
- Correct power connector to Pump 3 Activation Valve V7081-3 
If this does not fix the situation, Stop PVU.
- Check cables for valves HV7026-3 and HV7029-3 
- Check power to Pump 3 Activation Valve V7081-3 
- Check function of Pump 3 Activation Valve V7081-3 
- Check for failure in Pump 3 Activation Valve OK status signal, XC7083-3 or cabling.
- Check shutdown signal and cabling from ships Gas Safety System to all PVU control valves, V7081.
- Check hydraulic oil for contamination with dirt, water or air,

alarms.data_tree_path: PVCU2->PVU Failure Handling->Pumps->Pump 1 Circ Temp Deviating->Pump 1 Circ Temp Deviating Alarm
alarms.long_description: Pump 1 Circulation Temperature, TT7058-1  deviates too much from circulation temperature of the other 2 pumps. PVU cannot operate.
alarms.cause:
- Not enough flow through pump.
- - Manual valves HV7026-1 or HV7029-1 partly or fully closed, 
- - Orifices inside or after pump 1 clogged,
- Failure of pump 1 heat tracing.
- Failure of Pump 1 Circulation Temperature, TT7058-1  measurement.
alarms.effect: - If PVU was in operation, it has changed to Standby-fail state.\n- PVU cannot be started until pump 1 is sufficiently cooled.
alarms.suggested_action:
- Check position of manual valves HV7015 or HV7053,
- Check position of manual valves HV7026-1 or HV7029-1   
- Check positon of valves in return pipe to tank,
Stop PVU:
- Check function of Circulation Valve, V7050,
- Check the Pump 1 Circulation Temperature sensor, 7058-1  and cabling,
- Check  if orifices inside or after pump 1 are clogged,
Pump 1 can be blocked to get the PVU in operation using only 2 pumps.

alarms.long_description: Pumps Circulation Temperatures, TT7058-1/2/3, of the 2 pumps in operation deviates too much. PVU cannot operate.
alarms.cause:
- Not enough flow through one or both of the pumps,
- - Manual valves HV7026-x or HV7029-x partly or fully closed,

- Failure of pump x heat tracing.

alarms.effect: - PVU has changed to standby-fail.\n- PVU cannot be started before pump circulation temperatures are within allowed deviation.
alarms.suggested_action:
- Check position of manual valves HV7026-x or HV7029-x,  
- Check pumps heat tracing, 
- Compare N2 Sealing Temperatures, TT7097-1/2/3, of the 3 pumps,
Stop PVU:
- Check Pumps Circulation Temperature sensors, 7058-x, and cabling,
- Check if orifices inside or after pumps are clogged.

alarms.data_tree_path: PVCU2->PVU Failure Handling->Pumps->Int N2 Above Seal N2 dp Low->Int N2 Above Seal N2 dp Low
alarms.long_description: Pumps Intermediate Chamber Nitrogen Pressure, PT7093, is too low compared to Pumps Nitrogen Sealing Pressure, PT7096.
alarms.cause:
-Manual valve, HV7098, is failure closed,
- Manual valve, HV7090, is failure closed,
- Manual Valve, HV70011, hydraulic drain tank is failure opened,
- Control valve, V7091, is failure closed,
- Loss of nitrogen supply,
- Nitrogen vent outlet V30 is blocked,
- Failure of pressure regulator PCV7092 or PCV7095, 
- Leakage of pumps Intermediate chambers or nitrogen pipes,
- Failure of Nitrogen Sealing Pressure, PT7096, or Intermediate Chamber Nitrogen Pressure, PT7093, measurement.
alarms.effect: - If PVU was in operation, it has changed to Standby-fail state.\n- PVU cannot be started until pressure in PT7093 greater than PT7096.
alarms.suggested_action:
- Check that manual valves, HV7090 and HV7098, is open,
- Check that manual valve, HV70011, of hydraulic drain tank is closed, 
- Check position of control valve, V7091, power, cabling and function, 
- Check nitrogen supply pressure externally to PVU, 
- Check if nitrogen vent outlet V30 is blocked,
- Check pressure regulators PCV7095 and PCV7092, function and adjustment,
- Check Pumps Intermediate Chambers or nitrogen pipes for leakages, 
- Check sensor and cabling of Nitrogen Seal Pressure sensor, PT7096, and Intermediate Chamber Nitrogen Pressure sensor, PT7093.

alarms.long_description: Circulation Valve, V7050, position signal, ZT7051, indicates that valve is more closed than commanded by setpoint. PVU cannot operate.
alarms.cause:
- Failure of position control of Circulation Valve V7050,
- - Failure of Circulation Valve, V7050, position measurement, ZT7051,
- - - Wrong adjustment of position sensor, ZT7051,
- - - - Position signal is wrong, when Circulation Valve hits mechanical fully Open end stop,
- - Failure of Circulation Valve Setpoint signal XC7050,
- - Failure of Circulation Valve position controller, 
- - Low Control Air Pressure, PT7067. 

 In case of an external shutdown, XC7192, the position of V7050 can be drifting away from the setpoint, as the control air pressure is dumped. This is not a failure.
alarms.effect: PVU pressure is blown down and PVU stopped.\nPVU cannot operate before the failure situation is fixed.
alarms.suggested_action:
- Check Circulation Valve, V7050, its position sensor, ZT7051, position controller and cabling,
- Check calibration of Circulation Valve Position sensor, ZT7051,
- Check Control Air Pressure, PT7067,
- Check Circulation Valve Setpoint signal, XC7050, on PVCU3, ch. 71, and cabling,
- Check Circulation Valve Position signal, ZT7051, on PVCU2, ch. 34.

alarms.data_tree_path: PVCU3->System->24V Power Supervision->ECS Insulation Level Supervision->ECS Insulation level below normal
alarms.long_description: PVCU3 electric insulation level is below normal service value.
alarms.cause: One or more components connected to PVCU3 have increased electric leakage to ships ground.
alarms.effect: No immediate effect. The alarm can be an indication of beginning deterioration of system components.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Insulation level by observing: Maintenance -> Troubleshooting -> Insulation,
- Insulation level trend in CoCoS-EDS if applicable,
- Individual insulation of PVCU3 components (sensors, controllers, actuators, cabling) to determine the cause of leakage.

alarms.data_tree_path: PVCU3->System->24V Power Supervision->ECS Insulation Level Supervision->ECS Insulation level too low
alarms.long_description: PVCU3 electric insulation level is too low.
alarms.cause: One or more components connected to PVCU3 have too high electric leakage to ships ground.
alarms.effect:
- The systems resistance against electrical noise is reduced.
- Additional insulation faults on opposite polarity can cause blown fuses or short circuits.
NOTE:
Never ignore this alarm. Safety critical issues may arise.
alarms.suggested_action:
NOTE:
Never ignore this alarm. Safety critical issues may arise.
Check:
- Insulation level by observing : Maintenance -> Troubleshooting -> Insulation,
- Insulation level trend in CoCoS-EDS if applicable,
- Individual insulation of PVCU3 components (sensors, controllers, actuators, cabling) to determine the cause of leakage.

alarms.data_tree_path: PVCU3->System->24V Power Supervision->1390-PS-Failed Channel
alarms.long_description: I/O Channel Failed.
alarms.cause: Hardware failure in the I/O channel.
alarms.effect: May reduce performance.
alarms.suggested_action:
Try the steps below until OK. For each step check whether the error has disappeared:
   1) Check that all screws holding the modules are securely fastened
   2) Replace the corresponding module
   3) Replace CPU module
   4) Replace the controller frame, containing the back plane.

alarms.data_tree_path: PVCU3->System->24V Power Supervision->1390-PS-Module unavail.
alarms.long_description: I/O Module Unavailable
alarms.cause: Module is not connected correct or Module has damaged HW.
alarms.effect: May reduce performance.
alarms.suggested_action: Replace corresponding Triton module.

alarms.data_tree_path: PVCU3->System->Packet loss monitor->Alarm->Packet loss detected
alarms.long_description: Packet loss detected within last minute.
alarms.cause: Network is not performing optimally.
alarms.effect: Communication between nodes is not working optimally.
alarms.suggested_action:
Please check network cables for bad connections.
The problem can be further isolated by using the Network Status screen:
1) Go to Maintenance -> Network Status
2) Press Status Views and select between any of the 4 Network Quality buttons
Network paths with lost packets observed within the last minute, last hour, last 24 hours or since last reset will then be indicated on the screen.

alarms.long_description: The function should be cut-out in PVU
alarms.cause: The function is not cut-out in PVU
alarms.effect: None. PVU continues operation.
alarms.suggested_action: Contact MAN-ES if occurring

alarms.data_tree_path: *->System->Global Params. inconsist
alarms.long_description: Global parameter deviation. One or more parameters, the system expects to have the same value, differ.
alarms.cause: - If a user has adjusted a parameter at the MOP, one or more units have not received or accepted the change.\n- Configuration error.
alarms.effect: - Performance may be affected.\n- Redundancy may be reduced.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check that all controllers are in normal running mode.

If any parameter has been adjusted recently, repeat the adjustment.

If the suggested actions do not solve the inconsistency, then contact MAN ES.

alarms.data_tree_path: PVCU3->System->DR,2202,Alarm relay Digital Out->SRELAY-Alarm relay Digital Out-Failed Channel
alarms.long_description: I/O Channel Failed.
alarms.cause: Hardware failure in the I/O channel.
alarms.effect: May reduce performance.
alarms.suggested_action:
Try the steps below until OK. For each step check whether the error has disappeared:
   1) Check that all screws holding the modules are securely fastened
   2) Replace the corresponding module
   3) Replace CPU module
   4) Replace the controller frame, containing the back plane.

alarms.suggested_action: Please check cables and HW connected to the I/O\nReenable the channel via the UI on the CPU module, once the problem has been fixed.\nReplace the module if the problem persists or if no problem external to the module is found.
